chapter: The levee club and the St. Louis scene
title: Armstrong at the Paradise; Floyd Campbell and the Creath-Moten baseball dance
summary: Thomas recalls Armstrong's appearance with Floyd Campbell's band at the Paradise, Floyd Campbell as a blues singer, and a 1926 baseball-and-dance night pitting Creath's band against Bennie Moten's.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: They both knew it because I told them about it. Now in ... one night a little thing happened. Around '28 now I had my think, Stan. And, I bought my new suit on time and mother little chick with me, fine, you know. Louis Armstrong had done an afternoon in a place, in a ballroom called the Paradise. He How in the hell I remember that, I don't know but anyhow it happened. Beautifully. He played with the Floyd Campbell (?) band making a personal appearance. And we went to ... 'cause money, scratch is Christ, you're getting short here.
Was Floyd Campbell's a St. Louis band?
Floyd Campbell, I think, was one of the greatest blues singer I ever heard.

Yeah. I often told talking about the late, great Jimmy Rushing (?) about him and a the situation that has developed in, I think, it was '26 .../The Kansas City Monarch's were playing the St. Louis Stars, a baseball game. In those days, they'd have a baseball game and a dance. Benny Moten (?) was the big band in Kansas City.

Charlie Creath was the big band in St. Louis. And I talked to Jimmy Rushing about that one day. We got to laughing about it. And he always mentioned Floyd Campbell's singing. Now what happened was the St. Louis Stars beat the Kansas City -- what was the Kansas City team? Good team. Fellows like Page ( ? . ) Great team. And, Charlie Creath watched Benny Moten over here. They stretched the ... I hate to laugh about it. Nobody would talk about it. And not really ...
This was around '26 but Creath's band ...

No, I would say -- well, you may allow for a couple of years, maybe '26, it could be. Jimmy Rushing I had a lot of respect for Jimmy Rushing ... We never recorded together ... I don't think Basie was in that band at that time.
But you're thinking about you can't classify people, there's a difference of approach to everybody's ideas so who think can compare one with the other. I can't, you know.
